verdicts.what_goes_wrong: capture_output=True silently replaces caller stdout/stderr and input= raises TypeError from Popen, unlike the documented subprocess.run behavior.
verdicts.evidence: puppetmaster/codegraph.py:114-118 sets stdout/stderr=PIPE and calls subprocess.Popen(command, **kwargs). Docstring line 107 says it is subprocess.run 'with one difference at a timeout'; docs/CHANGELOG.md v1.51.1: 'has the signature of subprocess.run'. All five callers (codegraph.py:430, 452, 519, 868, 1651) pass stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True and no stdout/stderr/input.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: When the pin was resolved against a registry set by PUPPETMASTER_MODELS_PATH or a payload registry_path, the hint commands have no --registry-path, so a user who runs them in a shell without that env syncs or enables ~/.puppetmaster/models.json and the failing registry stays unrepaired.
verdicts.evidence: routing_authority.py:92 path = registry_path or registry_path_from_payload(payload, allow_default=True) (payload registry_path or default_registry_path(), which honors $PUPPETMASTER_MODELS_PATH, model_registry.py:225); orchestrator.py:1957 calls it for every explicit pin. registry_sync.py:203-212 emits `puppetmaster models sync --apply` and enable_command(id) with no registry path; models sync takes --registry-path (cli/_parser.py:2676).

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A pin on a starter id whose identity the registry has under another id fails with a hint to run `models sync --apply`, but sync lists it as covered and adds nothing, so the user follows a repair that does nothing.
verdicts.evidence: Probed on project/: registry [claude-code/my-haiku with adapter_model_name claude-haiku-5-5]; resolve_model_pin('claude-code/haiku-5-5') -> None (exact id only, normalized tail 'haiku-5-5' != 'claude-haiku-5-5'); unroutable_pin_hint returns "'claude-code/haiku-5-5' is a starter registry entry that this registry does not have. Run `puppetmaster models sync` ... --apply to add them."; plan_starter_sync returns covered [('claude-code/haiku-5-5','claude-code/my-haiku')] and no addition. registry_sync.py:194-196 looks up present only by spec.id; registry_sync.py:115-118 skips covered ids. Path: orchestrator.py:1957 -> routing_authority.py:95-99.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A starter spec that is already not routable would be appended without the models_sync disabled_reason and disabled_authority that the module docstring promises.
verdicts.evidence: registry_sync.py:82 `if not spec.is_routable or (enable and not adapter_locked): return spec`; module docstring lines 13-15 say the default entry gets disabled_reason naming `puppetmaster models sync` and disabled_authority models_sync. Probed: [s for s in starter_registry() if not s.is_routable] == [], so no starter entry reaches the branch today.

cli/commands_models.py:742-743 prints 'puppetmaster models set <id> enabled=true disabled_reason= disabled_authority=', which is byte-equal to registry_sync.enable_command('<id>') (registry_sync.py:74-78) today; no output is wrong. Owner decision: whether the duplicated text must be replaced by enable_command('<id>') to keep one source.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: input= raises TypeError from Popen instead of feeding stdin as subprocess.run does.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:118 subprocess.Popen(command, **kwargs) and :120 process.communicate(timeout=timeout) with no input; CHANGELOG v1.51.1 'has the signature of subprocess.run'. No caller passes input= (codegraph.py:430, 452, 519, 868, 1651 all pass stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL).

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: For a staged rename of a file whose name contains ' -> ', the CodeGraph freshness report lists a fragment such as 'b.txt" -> c.txt' in changed_sample in place of the destination path.
verdicts.evidence: Probed: git status --porcelain gives 'R  "a -> b.txt" -> c.txt' after `git mv "a -> b.txt" c.txt`; _porcelain_path returns 'b.txt" -> c.txt' (codegraph.py:1721-1722 splits on the first ' -> '); _git_changes_since returned (['b.txt" -> c.txt'], 1, False, 1). Reached from codegraph_freshness (codegraph.py:1849) via `puppetmaster codegraph` freshness (cli/commands_codegraph.py:233) and MCP (mcp_server.py:2034). The count stays correct because the stat failure counts it as changed.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A pin on a starter id that the registry has disabled under a custom id gets the 'absent, run models sync --apply' hint, and sync skips it as covered, so the hint does not name the disabled entry or its enable command.
verdicts.evidence: Probed on project/: registry [claude-code/my-haiku, enabled=False]; unroutable_pin_hint('claude-code/haiku-5-5' and 'claude-haiku-5-5') both return the absent text; plan_starter_sync returns covered [('claude-code/haiku-5-5','claude-code/my-haiku')]. registry_sync.py:194-196 exact-id lookup.

registry_sync.py module docstring: 'An entry on an adapter that the platform lock disables is always written with enabled: false.' docs/MODEL_ROUTING.md: 'With --enable ... An entry on an adapter that the platform lock disables always gets enabled: false' and 'A write changes the registry digest. A task with a model pin that was queued before the write fails at dispatch. Start it again.' tests/test_registry_sync.py:311 test_doctor_is_ok_after_apply: the warning clears after one apply, so it is not permanent, and the digest change is documented.
